items.followUp: What protocol is used to receive email from a mail server?

rubric.why: Identifies what SMTP stands for.
rubric.description: Expands the acronym SMTP.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct full form.

rubric.why: Shows the protocol’s main purpose.
rubric.description: Explains that SMTP is used to send email, including between mail servers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that SMTP sends email.

modelAnswer: SMTP stands for Simple Mail Transfer Protocol.
It is used to send email from a user’s device to a mail server and between mail servers.

items.followUp: How many layers are in the OSI model, and what are the names of its layers?

rubric.why: Gives the layer count for the OSI model.
rubric.description: States that the OSI model has seven layers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the OSI model and its seven layers.

rubric.why: Gives the layer count for the TCP/IP model.
rubric.description: States that the TCP/IP model has four layers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the TCP/IP model and its four layers.

modelAnswer: The OSI network model has 7 layers.
The TCP/IP network model has 4 layers.

items.followUp: Define an algorithm and write one advantage and one disadvantage of using it.

rubric.why: Checks that the answer defines a flowchart as a visual representation of a process or algorithm.
rubric.description: Defines a flowchart.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a flowchart as a diagram using symbols to show the steps of an algorithm or process.

rubric.why: Checks for a valid advantage of flowcharts.
rubric.description: Gives one advantage, such as making program logic easier to understand or communicate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one relevant advantage.

rubric.why: Checks for a valid disadvantage of preparing or using flowcharts.
rubric.description: Gives one disadvantage, such as taking time to draw or becoming difficult to manage when complex.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one relevant disadvantage.

rubric.why: Rewards an additional distinct benefit or use of a flowchart.
rubric.description: Adds a further valid advantage, such as helping plan, document, or check program logic.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a distinct relevant advantage.

modelAnswer: A flowchart is a diagram that uses standard symbols and arrows to show the steps and flow of an algorithm or process.
Advantages: It makes program logic easier to understand and communicate, and helps in planning and checking a solution.
Disadvantages: Drawing a flowchart can take time, and a large or complex flowchart can be difficult to follow or modify.

items.followUp: Name the components of a communication system and briefly describe any two.

rubric.why: Identifies the origin of the communication.
rubric.description: Names the sender or source.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the sender as the person or device that sends the message.

rubric.why: Identifies the intended recipient.
rubric.description: Names the receiver or destination.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the receiver as the person or device that receives the message.

rubric.why: Identifies what is communicated.
rubric.description: Names the message or data being sent.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the information being communicated.

rubric.why: Identifies a means or rule used to carry out communication.
rubric.description: Names a transmission medium/channel or communication protocol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a valid medium, channel, or protocol.

modelAnswer: The main components of a communication system are sender, receiver, message, transmission medium (channel), and protocol.
The sender creates and sends the message; the receiver gets it.
The message is the information being communicated, and the medium carries it from sender to receiver.
Protocols are the rules that govern communication between devices.

items.followUp: What is plagiarism, and why should it be avoided?

rubric.why: Checks that copyright is described as a legal right belonging to a creator or owner.
rubric.description: Defines copyright as a legal right over a creator’s work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying copyright as a legal right or ownership right.

rubric.why: Checks that the answer identifies the kinds of work protected.
rubric.description: States that copyright protects original works, such as writing, music, art, or software.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying original creative work as the subject of copyright.

rubric.why: Checks the protection against copying or use without permission.
rubric.description: Explains that copyright restricts unauthorized copying, reproduction, or distribution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that copying or use requires permission.

rubric.why: Checks that the answer recognizes the rights or credit of the creator/owner.
rubric.description: Mentions that copyright helps protect the creator’s rights or control over their work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant statement about protecting the creator or owner.

modelAnswer: Copyright is the legal right of a creator or owner over an original work, such as a book, song, picture, or software.
It protects the work from being copied, reproduced, distributed, or used without the owner’s permission.
Copyright helps creators control how their work is used and receive proper credit for it.

items.followUp: What is computer vandalism, and give one example of it.

rubric.why: Checks that sabotage is intentional and harmful.
rubric.description: Identifies sabotage as deliberate or malicious action.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the action is intentional or malicious.

rubric.why: Checks that the answer describes harm to a computer system or its operation.
rubric.description: Explains that sabotage damages, destroys, or disrupts a computer system or its data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the harmful effect.

rubric.why: Checks that the target is computer-related.
rubric.description: Identifies a computer, network, software, or data as the target.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a relevant target.

rubric.why: Checks for a concrete example of sabotage.
rubric.description: Gives a relevant example, such as deleting data or deliberately disrupting a network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid example.

modelAnswer: Computer sabotage is the deliberate or malicious act of damaging or disrupting a computer system, network, software, or data.
For example, a person may deliberately delete important files or use malware to disrupt a network.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of debugging a program?

rubric.why: Checks that testing is described as an examination of a program while it runs or is used.
rubric.description: States that testing involves running or checking a program with data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing testing as checking or running the program.

rubric.why: Checks that testing helps reveal faults and supports confidence in the program’s behavior.
rubric.description: Explains that testing helps find errors and check that the program produces correct results or meets requirements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying error detection or checking correct operation.

modelAnswer: Testing is important because it helps find errors or bugs in a program.
It also checks that the program works correctly and meets its requirements before it is used.

items.followUp: In an algorithm, what notations can be used to show processing and output?

rubric.why: Checks the notation used to obtain data for an algorithm.
rubric.description: Explains that input notation, such as INPUT or READ, accepts data for processing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing input notation.

rubric.why: Checks the notation used to present an algorithm’s result.
rubric.description: Explains that output notation, such as OUTPUT, WRITE, or PRINT, presents results.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing output notation.

modelAnswer: Input notation (such as INPUT or READ) shows that data is entered into an algorithm.
Output notation (such as OUTPUT, WRITE, or PRINT) shows that the result is displayed or produced.
